transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~63 minutes
Location: All-hands (Zoom)
Attendees: Asha, Samir, Maya, Evan, Lena + company

Summary:
Asha reviews company performance for Q1, hiring and offsite logistics; Samir covers runtime and infrastructure wins including 2x throughput improvements on common configs; Maya outlines product roadmap priorities for Q2 (Dedicated autoscaling, Private deployment GA, Optimize enhancements); Lena covers go-to-market metrics and upcoming enterprise pushes; leadership Q&A follows.

Topics:
- Q1 results & topline metrics
- Performance and cost improvements in serving runtime
- Product priorities: Dedicated autoscaling, Private GA, Optimize features
- Hiring update and offsite announcement
- Security and compliance: SOC2 progress

Action items (brief): see metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Asha: Hey everyone, good morning, good afternoon, wherever you are. Uh, welcome to the April all-hands. We, uh, have quite a bit to cover so we'll keep things tight. Quick housekeeping; we'll record, slides will be shared, and Q&A at the end.

[00:28] Samir: Morning. I'm gonna kick off with a quick infra update — we shipped the new kernel selection heuristics last month, and in our internal perf tests it's roughly two x throughput on the 4k/8k sequence mix for the quantized M-family we tested. Caveat, yeah, this is internal bench, so, uh, take with the usual grain.

[01:02] Maya: And that improvement is already visible in Dedicated beta customers, like the POC with Orion Health — they're seeing lower tail latency and fewer OOMs in burst. There were, uh, some tuning knobs we had to press, and we'll roll those into a config toggle in the console.

[01:40] Evan: To add, our autoscaler work is also reduced cold-starts by, hmm, about 30% in our staging runs when combined with the new KV cache heuristics. There's still work: edge cases for very spiky workloads, but the baseline is promising.

[02:10] Asha: Nice. On the business side, Lena, can you walk through bookings and ARR?

[02:18] Lena: Sure. Quick snapshot: ARR up 26% quarter-over-quarter, net new bookings exceeded plan by about 12% thanks to two mid-market deals. Renewal health looks solid; churn is low; pipeline conversion improved after the new benchmark materials. We still have a couple larger enterprise decisions in legal — target close for those in May.

[03:02] Audience question (generic): Is the pricing change rolled out?

[03:08] Lena: Yes the new unit economics pricing for hosted API went live two weeks ago. We'll share a short FAQ in #announcements to help internal folks answer customer questions.

[03:28] Samir: On security/compliance, ops: we're on track for SOC 2 readiness, control docs are in the security repo, and the vendor audit kickoff is next week. Also, we updated our KMS integration to support a bring-your-own-key flow in Private deployments — still early but looks solid in testing.

[04:05] Maya: Product priorities for Q2. High-level: 1) Dedicated autoscaling GA, 2) Private deployment GA for our EU region with additional residency options, 3) Optimize: improved quantization recommendations and caching suggestions surfaced in the Console.

[04:35] Asha: Quick clarification on Private GA — that includes VPC peering and HSM KMS support?

[04:42] Maya: Yes, VPC peering and KMS/HSM integration are in scope. HSM requires the new onboarding checklist and legal updates. We're aligning the rollout with the enterprise sales pipeline.

[05:10] Evan: From engineering, we have two cross-team initiatives: kernel selection rollout and observability retention. The latter is to reduce query cost while allowing longer debug windows for customers on Premium tiers. We're drafting an RFC.

[05:36] Asha: Hiring update — we're at ~150 heads, engineering continues to ramp, and we're prioritizing infra, reliability, and product. People Ops will follow up with a recruiter blitz next week; also reminder about the optional remote offsite in July, please fill out the survey.

[06:00] Crowd mumble / brief applause

[06:10] Q&A start:
[06:12] Employee 1: Hi, quick question on latency — the 2x throughput you mentioned, does that change tail latency?

[06:18] Samir: Great question. The throughput gains are mostly at median; tail latency improvements depend on workload — for smaller batch sizes tail is better, but extremely chatty workloads with short-turn requests can see negligible improvements unless we enable some of the new batching policies. We'll post a short note with examples.

[06:50] Employee 2: Any change to the hosted SLA or rate limits with the new pricing?

[06:58] Lena: No SLA changes right now — same uptime target. Rate limits are configurable per account; sales will surface changes on a case-by-case when migrating customers to the new pricing.

[07:20] Employee 3: Are we open-sourcing the kernel selection heuristics?

[07:28] Samir: We're planning to publish parts of the heuristics as a recipe blog post — not the whole production engine, but examples and benchmarks for community benefit.

[07:50] Asha: Ok, next segment is a short leadership panel — Samir and Maya dive deeper.

[07:55] Samir: (slides) Showed heatmap of seq-len distribution across customers; if you look at the left — uh the numbers are noisy — but the key point is many customers are peaky at 512 and at ~3k, so we tuned kernel selection to bias toward mixed workloads.

[08:30] Maya: Product priorities again, with owners and dates: Dedicated autoscaling (owner: Maya, ETA: end of May), Private EU GA (owner: Maya + Security, ETA: June), Optimize improvements (owner: Product PMs, ETA: phased through Q3).

[09:05] Evan: Technical note: we found a regression in one internal optimizer affecting L2 cache locality; patch is rolling to canary, expect rollback safeguards if we see perf dips.

[09:35] Employee 4: Any updates on the customer POC with Nimbus? They asked about on-prem options.

[09:42] Lena: Nimbus POC is going well; they requested an on-prem package and longer retention — we're negotiating support terms and a pilot contract. Legal is looped in.

[10:05] Audience side chatter

[10:12] Asha: Before we wrap, quick shout-outs: ops team for the weekend deploy, infra for the perf wins, and revops for the bookings push. Thank you.

[10:25] Final Q&A:

[10:27] Employee 5: Will we get a recording and the slides?

[10:28] Asha: Yes, slides and recording posted in #all-hands and an email to the company.

[10:35] Employee 6: Offsite question — is the company covering travel?

[10:38] People Ops (typed in chat): We will share guidelines; core attendance is company-covered, partners and +1 costs are handled separately.

[10:55] Asha: Great. Quick recap of next steps: Maya will share autoscaling timeline, Evan will publish perf RFC, Lena will send the booking snapshot, People Ops will finalize offsite logistics.

[11:05] Asha: Thanks everyone, end of all-hands.

[11:10] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors and shorthand; some speaker labels approximate. Deck link shared in chat: https://drive.example.com/redwood/april-allhands-deck (internal).
